done.why: By the end of the run I'd spent too many turns carrying things back and forth. Each treasure had to go the long way around, through the barred trap door and the one-item chimney, the thief had taken my trident, and I'd died twice. I was at 76 of 350 points, still a Novice, and doing the same chores again, so I stopped.

about: You plunder an empire underground and put the trophies in a glass case in a white house. It's a world that likes to say no politely, sometimes with a wink: no climbing chimneys unless you're Santa, no leaping into chasms, and the gothic door means nothing. The changes I noticed were all about carrying things. Dying scatters your belongings across the fields, a tidy somebody puts the lamp back, the chimney fits you, your lamp and one thing more, and the sword gets the blame when your load is too heavy.

moments.note: The room describes a boarded front door, but 'knock on the boarded door' got 'You can't see any such thing.' Later 'east' answered that the door is boarded, so the door exists for some commands and not others.
'I don't think that the leaflet would agree with you.' The first refusal with some charm.
The gothic lettering translates to 'This space intentionally left blank.'
Adding 'and admire it' produced 'Done.' and then 'You can't see any such thing.' A trailing clause or an adverb like 'anyway' kept breaking otherwise valid commands (turns 9, 55).
'roll up the rug' worked. The parser took a phrasing I didn't expect it to.
'offer the troll the lunch' worked and he ate it. Then 'give lunch to troll' said I couldn't see it, which is fair since he'd eaten it.
The death text is new: plain things are strewn about the forest and fields, valuables roll into a dark corner, and somebody tidy puts the lamp back. It turned dying into a scavenger hunt.
Opening the egg with the knife wrecked the canary, and the world kept that consequence. I liked it.
The chimney told me exactly what I was carrying and that it has 'room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.' A clear rule I could plan around.
I died a second time fighting the troll with only the knife because I couldn't find the sword after my first death.
I found the sword lying in the east clearing, well away from where I'd been looking. A small reward for wandering.
With the sword I took the troll's head off and the carcass vanished in black fog. Satisfying after two deaths.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' The game singled out the sword, which I read as a nudge.
I pressed the blue button just to be contrary and flooded the maintenance room. Then I patched the leak with the gunk from the tube, which felt like real low cunning.
The thief walked through the Mirror Room and took Poseidon's trident before I could do anything.
The trap door was locked from above, so every treasure had to go out the long way through the Studio chimney, one at a time.

wished: Knock on, pry or unboard the front door it keeps mentioning
Use adverbs or trailing clauses ('anyway', 'and admire it') without the parser choking
Climb the 'unclimbable' ramp or the 'impassable' mountains, or at least get a refusal written in the world's voice instead of 'That sentence isn't one I recognize'
Pick the grating lock with the knife
Walk on the rainbow just because I wanted to
Tie the rope to anything I tried
Unbar the trap door from below so I didn't have to keep shuttling through the chimney
Ask where my things went after dying

lines.line: Only Santa Claus climbs down chimneys.
lines.why: A refusal with a personality, which I want when I'm poking at the edges.

lines.line: The engravings translate to "This space intentionally left blank."
lines.why: A joke about a door that leads nowhere. It made me laugh and stop trying it.

lines.line: Your belongings, such as they were, have not come with you. The plain things are strewn about the forest and the fields around the house, anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: This reshaped the game for me after dying. Recovering my things became a hunt, and 'somebody tidy' is a nice touch.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A clear, fair rule, put plainly, that I then planned every trip around.

lines.line: Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.
lines.why: It singled out one item. I read it as the world telling me what to put down.

lines.line: It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head.
On the way through, he quietly abstracted some valuables from your possession, mumbling something about "Doing unto others before..."
lines.why: It stung, but it gave the thief a character.

fun.why: The fun peaks were the troll kill, flooding the room and then patching the leak, and finding my sword after the death scramble. Too much of the rest was walking treasures out through the chimney and losing the trident to the thief.

engagement.why: The new rules about dying and carrying kept me thinking and planning. Once those rules mostly meant long round trips (turns 233-265), my attention dropped.

difficulty.why: I died twice to the troll, then had to search the fields for my sword. Losing the trident and having the trap door locked from below made progress slow. It wasn't unfair, but it was punishing for someone who experiments.

interestingness.why: The changes are interesting: belongings scatter when you die, the chimney limits what you carry, and the game comments on your load. Even consequences of my contrariness stuck, like the wrecked canary.

prose.why: The written lines are witty and specific. Points off for the flat 'That sentence isn't one I recognize' and 'You can't see any such thing' whenever I phrased something oddly (turns 1, 7, 9, 39, 50, 55).
